network.overall_strategy: Use a mixed-resolution network centered on racemic proline. The cyanosulfidic Patel branch is expanded through experimentally identified intermediates because it is the most mechanistically explicit proline-specific route in the literature. Independent hydrothermal HCN/HCHO chemistry, thermal HCHO/NH3 condensation, and direct electric-discharge synthesis are included as stoichiometrically balanced overall route-family nodes supported by experiment. Two upstream methane-based source modules generate HCN/NH3 and HCHO/H2, allowing 10 distinct source-to-target pathways. Because the supplied literature does not establish abiotic L-selective proline synthesis, the final DL-proline to L-proline step is explicitly a speculative physical enrichment/resolution module.

reactions.name: Discharge fixation of methane and nitrogen to hydrogen cyanide and ammonia

conditions.other: Reducing CH4/N2 gas phase or gas-water interface; best treated as local/transient rather than global atmosphere chemistry.

reactions.mechanism: Electrical discharge fragments CH4 and N2 into radicals; recombination yields HCN and NH3.
reactions.reasoning: Reduced-gas discharge experiments on CH4/N2/H2O with traces of NH3 generated the HCN-rich chemistry from which amino acids, including proline, arise (Ring et al., 1972). HCN is also photochemically plausible in some N2-rich atmospheres (Rugheimer and Rimmer, 2019), and silicate/glass surfaces alter discharge product distributions (Criado-Reyes et al., 2021). The written stoichiometry is a lumped source step, not a claimed elementary process; a globally CH4-rich atmosphere remains contested (Trail et al., 2011).

reactions.name: Energetic methane-water conversion to formaldehyde and hydrogen

conditions.other: Speculative source-consolidation step for carbonyl formation and reducing-equivalent generation at a gas-water interface.

reactions.mechanism: Energetic activation of methane and water gives oxygen insertion to formaldehyde and release of H2.
reactions.reasoning: This is explicitly speculative as a source-consolidation node: the supplied proline papers use formaldehyde as a feedstock rather than isolating the exact net reaction written here. It is included because reduced-gas discharge chemistry does generate carbonyl species (Ring et al., 1972; Criado-Reyes et al., 2021), and formaldehyde is a recurrent precursor in both the Fox-Windsor and Hennet proline route families (Fox and Windsor, 1970; Hennet et al., 1992).

reactions.name: Cyanovinylation of acetylene to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: Cyanosulfidic shallow pond or evaporitic pool with UV irradiation.

reactions.mechanism: Cyanovinylation of acetylene gives acrylonitrile under photoredox conditions.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) place acrylonitrile at the entry point of the proline branch of cyanosulfidic chemistry. This is the most mechanistically explicit proline-specific route in the supplied literature, with UV/sulfide/Cu chemistry used to manage nitrile formation under surface conditions (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Ammonia addition to acrylonitrile
reactions.mechanism: Ammonia undergoes conjugate addition to the activated alkene/nitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Ammonia addition to acrylonitrile to give beta-aminopropionitrile was directly tracked in the Patel network, with high conversion reported. Unlike the older discharge and thermal routes, this intermediate is experimentally identified rather than merely inferred (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Reduction of beta-aminopropionitrile to 3-aminopropanal

conditions.other: UV photoreduction; H2 is used here as a net reducing-equivalent placeholder for sulfide-driven reduction.

reactions.mechanism: Net photoreductive conversion of the nitrile to an aldehyde, with hydrolytic loss of the nitrile nitrogen as NH3.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) experimentally converted beta-aminopropionitrile to 3-aminopropanal under UV-driven sulfide chemistry. In the balanced net written here, H2 is a bookkeeping proxy for the reducing equivalents delivered experimentally by HS- photoredox and geochemically by strongly reducing fluids; the stoichiometry is condensed, but the intermediate identity is literature-supported (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Cyanohydrin-thioamide cyclization to proline aminonitrile

conditions.other: Compressed representation of cyanohydrin, thioamide, cyclization, and reductive cyanation chemistry; H2 again denotes net reducing equivalents.

reactions.mechanism: 3-Aminopropanal forms a cyanohydrin, enters thioamide/cyclic thioamide chemistry, cyclizes, and is reductively cyanated to the cyclic aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) mapped 3-aminopropanal through cyanohydrin and thioamide chemistry, cyclization to a gamma-butyrothiolactam manifold, and final cyanide chemistry to a cyclic alpha-aminonitrile precursor of proline. This node compresses that experimentally supported manifold into one balanced net transformation while retaining the key structural anchors 3-aminopropanal and proline aminonitrile; environmental execution remains demanding because UV, cyanide, sulfide, and careful sequencing are all required (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of proline aminonitrile to rac-proline

conditions.other: Prolonged aqueous heating or wet-dry/geothermal cycling; stoichiometrically two waters are implied.

reactions.mechanism: Aqueous nitrile hydrolysis converts the cyclic alpha-aminonitrile to rac-proline.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) stop at the cyclic aminonitrile rather than quantifying free proline from the same sequence. Hydrolysis of alpha-aminonitriles to amino acids is chemically standard, so this step is plausible, but in the context of the Patel route it remains partly extrapolative rather than directly measured (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Hydrothermal HCN-formaldehyde synthesis of rac-proline

conditions.other: HCN/HCHO/NH4+-rich reducing flow with rapid quench favored over long high-temperature residence.

reactions.mechanism: Hot cyanide-carbonyl chemistry on Fe-S/clay minerals yields amino acids; proline emerges through unresolved network cyclization.
reactions.reasoning: Hennet et al. (1992) reported proline among amino acids formed from HCN/HCHO/NH4+ at about 150 C and 10 bar with pyrite-pyrrhotite-magnetite or illite. The present node is a balanced summary of that complex hydrothermal network rather than a resolved elementary mechanism; the authors did not claim their high precursor concentrations were natural, and amino-acid survival is strongly limited by temperature and residence time (Hennet et al., 1992; Bada et al., 1995; Yanagawa and Kobayashi, 1997).

reactions.name: Thermal formaldehyde-ammonia synthesis of rac-proline precursors

conditions.other: Thermal HCHO/NH3 condensate; experimentally the analyte was released after hydrolysis.

reactions.mechanism: Thermal carbonyl-ammonia condensation produces hydrolysable N-rich organics that release proline on hydrolysis.
reactions.reasoning: Fox and Windsor (1970) observed proline only after hydrolysis of a heated HCHO/NH3 product mixture. This node is therefore a balanced lumped representation of high-temperature aqueous condensation chemistry leading to proline-releasing material, not a directly observed one-step free-proline synthesis; hydrolysis-based assays require caution, as emphasized in related early work (Fox and Windsor, 1970; Wolman et al., 1971).

reactions.name: Direct Miller-type discharge synthesis of rac-proline

conditions.other: Strongly reducing discharge chemistry; experimentally proline was a minor product.

reactions.mechanism: Plasma radical chemistry generates a complex HCN/carbonyl-rich mixture from which a small proline branch emerges.
reactions.reasoning: Ring et al. (1972) directly detected proline in electric-discharge products from CH4/N2/H2O with trace NH3, but at low abundance and without a resolved ring-forming mechanism. This node encodes that route family as a balanced overall branch; surface effects on Miller-type chemistry are real, and a globally reducing atmosphere is disputed, so this is best treated as local/transient surface chemistry (Ring et al., 1972; Criado-Reyes et al., 2021; Trail et al., 2011).

reactions.name: Speculative resolution of rac-proline to L-proline

conditions.other: Formal node for selective adsorption, crystallization, or eutectic partitioning of a racemic pool; the complementary non-L phase is not explicitly represented.

reactions.mechanism: Physical partitioning of DL-proline into an L-enriched phase.
reactions.reasoning: No reaction in the supplied literature demonstrates strong abiotic L-selective synthesis of proline from achiral feedstocks. This node is therefore explicitly speculative and represents post-synthetic physical resolution or enrichment of a racemic proline pool, included only because the requested target is L-proline; the review emphasizes that prebiotic access to the proline skeleton is supported, whereas an L-selective module remains unsolved (Munoz Caro et al., 2002; Engel and Nagy, 1982; Patel et al., 2015).

pathways.name: Direct cyanosulfidic aminonitrile pathway
pathways.description: Patel-type surface chemistry from HCN and acetylene to the cyclic aminonitrile, followed by hydrolysis and a speculative L-enrichment step.

pathways.name: Atmospheric-HCN-fed cyanosulfidic pathway
pathways.description: Electric-discharge fixation supplies HCN/NH3 to the Patel branch; reducing equivalents are otherwise externally available.

pathways.name: Hydrogen-fed cyanosulfidic pathway
pathways.description: Methane-water energetic processing supplies reducing power as H2, which is then used in the Patel aminonitrile branch.

pathways.name: Dual-source atmospheric cyanosulfidic pathway
pathways.description: Methane-derived source modules provide both HCN/NH3 and H2 before entry into the Patel branch, then hydrolysis and speculative L-resolution follow.

pathways.name: Direct hydrothermal HCN-formaldehyde pathway
pathways.description: A vent-like HCN/HCHO network on Fe-S or clay minerals gives rac-proline directly, followed by speculative L-enrichment.

pathways.name: HCN-seeded hydrothermal pathway
pathways.description: Surface discharge supplies HCN, which then enters the hydrothermal HCN/HCHO proline-forming network before the final speculative resolution step.

pathways.name: Fully sourced hydrothermal pathway
pathways.description: Methane-derived source steps provide both HCN and HCHO before hydrothermal conversion to rac-proline and later speculative L-selection.

pathways.name: Direct thermal formaldehyde-ammonia pathway
pathways.description: Fox-Windsor-type high-temperature HCHO/NH3 condensation yields proline-releasing material summarized here as rac-proline, then a speculative L-enrichment step.

pathways.name: Methane-water-fed thermal pathway
pathways.description: A methane-water source step supplies formaldehyde to the thermal HCHO/NH3 route before the final speculative L-selection node.

pathways.name: Direct electric-discharge pathway
pathways.description: Low-yield Miller-type discharge chemistry gives rac-proline directly from simple gases and water, followed by a speculative post-synthetic L-enrichment step.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the most coherent route to the proline skeleton and aligns best with the mechanistic Patel literature up to the aminonitrile stage. rxn_003 and rxn_004 are well supported, rxn_005 is only a coarse net reduction node, and rxn_006 is too compressed to be chemically secure because the published route proceeds through cyanohydrin and sulfur-bearing thioamide/thiolactam intermediates under HS-, UV, and Cu chemistry. If rxn_006 is kept as a net node it should at least use the balanced stoichiometry with 2 HCN and 2 H2; rxn_007 also needs 2 H2O. The path can plausibly reach DL-proline, but rxn_011 does not provide an evidenced synthesis of L-proline.
suggestions: Split rxn_006 into explicit cyanohydrin, thioamide or thiolactam, and aminonitrile steps with HS-, UV, and Cu conditions.
Correct stoichiometries for rxn_006 and rxn_007.
Treat rxn_011 as a separate unresolved physical enrichment module or stop the pathway at DL-proline.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Adding rxn_001 gives a literature-backed discharge source for HCN and NH3, but the network does not justify transport and concentration of those products into the cyanosulfidic surface setting. The same Patel-branch weakness remains: rxn_006 is not credible as a sulfur-free single step, and rxn_011 is still unresolved. This is better viewed as a sourced DL-proline pathway than an L-proline pathway.
suggestions: Add an atmospheric deposition or concentration step for HCN and NH3 before the surface cyanosulfidic sequence.
Expand rxn_006 into Patel-style sulfur photochemistry and correct its net stoichiometry.
Relabel rxn_001 as atmospheric discharge rather than generic Surface.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Hydrogen sourcing via rxn_002 is only a coarse energetic source module and is not tightly tied to the cited proline experiments. The balanced form should be CH4 + H2O -> CH2O + 2 H2, and the handoff from this source chemistry to the Patel surface sequence is not specified. rxn_005 and rxn_006 still miss the documented HS-, UV, and Cu context, and rxn_011 remains speculative.
suggestions: Correct rxn_002 to CH4 + H2O -> CH2O + 2 H2 and specify the energetic context.
Add HS-, UV, and Cu chemistry to rxn_005 and rxn_006 or split them into explicit literature-backed steps.
Replace rxn_011 with a clearly marked external enrichment module.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the most fully sourced Patel variant, but also the most environmentally under-justified because discharge products and methane-water source chemistry are fed into a surface cyanosulfidic sequence without explicit deposition or concentration steps. rxn_002 needs the 2 H2 stoichiometry, and rxn_006 still omits the essential sulfur and photoredox part of the published mechanism. L-proline is not actually established because rxn_011 is unresolved.
suggestions: Insert explicit transfer and concentration nodes linking atmospheric source chemistry to the surface cyanosulfidic environment.
Correct rxn_002 and replace rxn_006 with explicit sulfur-bearing Patel intermediates.
Keep the pathway target at DL-proline unless an evidenced enantioenrichment mechanism is added.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Reasonable as a hydrothermal route-family summary to rac-proline, since HCN and formaldehyde hydrothermal experiments do report minor proline. However rxn_008 is not a mechanistic one-step synthesis and should be interpreted only as an overall node; the balanced net form is 3 HCN + 6 CH2O -> C5H9NO2 + 2 NH3 + 4 CO. The literature also uses NH4+ and reducing minerals at about 150 C and 10 bar, which are absent here, and rxn_011 does not solve L-selectivity.
suggestions: Represent rxn_008 explicitly as an HCN and HCHO and NH4+ and mineral hydrothermal route-family node rather than a single resolved reaction.
Correct the rxn_008 stoichiometry and note the mineral and pressure context from the literature.
Keep the target at DL-proline unless an evidenced L-enrichment process is supplied.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Adding rxn_001 gives a plausible HCN source, but there is still no explicit deposition or concentration step from atmospheric discharge into the hydrothermal reactor. rxn_008 remains an overall route-family node rather than a resolved mechanism, and rxn_011 is speculative. This is better aligned with the literature as a sourced rac-proline pathway than as a route to L-proline.
suggestions: Add deposition and concentration of atmospheric HCN into the hydrothermal setting.
Add NH4+ and mineral redox buffers to the rxn_008 description and correct its stoichiometry.
Separate L-enrichment from synthesis.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Structurally complete, but environmentally weakest of the hydrothermal variants because both discharge and methane-water source modules are piped into hydrothermal chemistry without an explicit transport or concentration step. Correct rxn_002 and rxn_008 stoichiometries, add NH4+ and mineral context to rxn_008, and keep L-enrichment separate from synthesis.
suggestions: Correct rxn_002 and rxn_008 stoichiometries.
Insert transfer and concentration steps from atmospheric source chemistry to hydrothermal fluids.
Do not treat rxn_011 as established prebiotic chemistry.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Supported only at the route-family level. Fox-Windsor type chemistry gives proline mainly after hydrolysis of heated HCHO and NH3 products, so rxn_009 overstates the evidence by making free DL-proline directly. The balanced overall form is 6 CH2O + NH3 -> C5H9NO2 + CO + 3 H2O, but a proline-releasing precursor node would align better with the literature; rxn_011 remains unsupported.
suggestions: Change rxn_009 to a proline-releasing precursor or hydrolysate node, not direct free proline.
Correct rxn_009 stoichiometry and move the environment to a thermal aqueous or evaporative setting if that is what is intended.
Separate L-enrichment from synthesis.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Adding rxn_002 does not fix the main issue with the thermal route, which is that the literature supports hydrolysable precursor mixtures more clearly than direct free proline. rxn_002 needs CH4 + H2O -> CH2O + 2 H2, rxn_009 needs the 6 to 1 stoichiometry, and an environmental link between source chemistry and the thermal condensation setting is missing. L-proline is still not achieved.
suggestions: Correct rxn_002 and rxn_009 stoichiometries.
Add a transfer or concentration step linking methane-water source chemistry to the thermal condensation setting.
Represent the product as a hydrolysable precursor mixture unless direct free-proline evidence is supplied.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Direct discharge has real literature support for racemic proline in complex product mixtures, so this is a defensible overall route-family node. Still, rxn_010 is not a resolved mechanism, should be balanced as 5 CH4 + 3 N2 + 2 H2O -> C5H9NO2 + 5 NH3, and closer literature alignment would mention trace NH3, low proline yield, and the debated reducing atmosphere. rxn_011 remains an unsupported resolution step.
suggestions: Keep rxn_010 as a low-yield discharge route-family node and correct its stoichiometry.
Specify atmospheric discharge conditions and note the reducing-atmosphere limitation from the literature.
Treat L-resolution as unresolved rather than achieved.

evaluation.network_feedback: Network validity is good: the graph is connected, molecule IDs are consistent, and the supplied balance check reports no true conservation violations. However six reactions need explicit coefficients: rxn_002 CH4 + H2O -> CH2O + 2 H2; rxn_006 C3H7NO + 2 HCN + 2 H2 -> C5H8N2 + NH3 + H2O; rxn_007 C5H8N2 + 2 H2O -> C5H9NO2 + NH3; rxn_008 3 HCN + 6 CH2O -> C5H9NO2 + 2 NH3 + 4 CO; rxn_009 6 CH2O + NH3 -> C5H9NO2 + CO + 3 H2O; rxn_010 5 CH4 + 3 N2 + 2 H2O -> C5H9NO2 + 5 NH3. Literature alignment is fair to good: the network correctly treats Patel's branch as the most explicit proline-specific route and acknowledges that abiotic L-selective proline synthesis is not established. The main chemical weakness is rxn_006, which invokes thioamide chemistry without any sulfur species and collapses the documented HS-, UV, and Cu sequence too aggressively; rxn_005 is also under-specified. The hydrothermal, thermal, and discharge nodes are acceptable only as route-family summary nodes, with rxn_009 overstating the literature because Fox-Windsor mainly observed proline after hydrolysis of thermal products. Environmental consistency is mixed because atmospheric discharge steps are labeled Surface, hydrothermal conditions omit NH4+ and mineral buffers, and rxn_007 and rxn_011 are labeled Biochemical without a justified prebiotic setting. The network reaches DL-proline plausibly through several literature-backed families, but it does not yet demonstrate L-proline because rxn_011 is an unresolved enrichment and resolution module. Best interpreted as a rac-proline network with an external homochirality problem still open.
